# Workflow fixtures (Wave 4, Lane K)

- `envelope-good.json` - a completed golden run in the `flauz.tasks/v0` task envelope
  shape (produced by the real flauz-workspace services; validates via
  `validateEnvelope`).
- `workflow-good.json` - the matching `flauz.workflows/v1` fragment (produced by
  `distillTaskToFragment`).
- `bad/*.json` - one violated validation rule per file; consumed by
  `extensions/flauz-workflow/test/fixtures.test.ts`, which asserts each is
  rejected by `validateWorkflowFragment` with the expected rule message.
- `keys/` - the DL-20 signed-checkpoint fixture keystore: an Ed25519 keypair
  seed-derived from sha256('flauz-fixture-ed25519-1') plus an HMAC-SHA256 key
  from sha256('flauz-fixture-hmac-1'), described by `keys.json` (manifest
  format consumed by `loadCheckpointSigner`). DETERMINISTIC: regeneration via
  `generateFixtureKeystore()` is byte-identical (pinned by test).
  These stand in for the real user keystore - never use them for anything real.
- `ledger/` - the hardened-ledger fixtures (DL-20 Wave-4 hook), generated by
  `node extensions/flauz-workflow/test/generateLedgerFixtures.ts`
  (deterministic; committed output = regeneration):
  - `good.jsonl` + `good-size.json`: rows 1-4 (notes), row 5 (signed
    checkpoint covering row 4), row 6 (note); watermark rowCount 6.
  - `bad/forged-checkpoint*`: row 5's checkpoint signature flipped AND row 6's
    prev re-linked - a forger who recomputes the chain; only the signature
    check catches it (tamper class 7).
  - `bad/truncated-tail*`: final row dropped, stale watermark survives
    (tamper class 6, truncated).
  - `bad/last-row-tamper*`: final row's uri mutated in place, same byte length
    - the chain walks clean, only the watermark head catches it (the v0
    last-row limitation, CLOSED).
  - `bad/watermark-mismatch*`: good rows, one hex char of the watermark's
    headSha256 flipped (mismatch without truncation).
  Size fixtures are tab-indented per repo hygiene; runtime `.flauz/evidence/size.json`
  serializes 2-space canonical (DL-9) - JSON parsing is indent-agnostic.
- Fixture JSON is tab-indented per repo hygiene; the canonical 2-space
  serialization discipline is pinned by the envelope unit tests.
- A2A message fixtures land with the messaging milestone (see REPORT.md).
